accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Vishnuvardhana IV:
1. He backed Govinda III in the Rashtrakuta succession war.
2. He was defeated by Dhruva.
3. Dhruva married his daughter Sheela Mahadevi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Vishnuvardhana IV supported Govinda III, was defeated by Dhruva, and strengthened the relationship through Dhruva's marriage to Sheela Mahadevi.
accepted.tq: Combine the ruler, opponent and marriage-alliance facts before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: Vijayaditya II is traditionally associated with which of the following achievements?
o: Winning 18 battles in one regnal year
accepted.x: Vijayaditya II is traditionally said to have fought 108 battles in 12 years. The 108 temples were commemorative constructions associated with these victories.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive number with the correct activity rather than with a related monument or inscription.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: The 108 temples traditionally associated with Vijayaditya II were intended to commemorate his
accepted.x: The 108 temples commemorated Vijayaditya II's victories, traditionally connected with his 108 battles fought over 12 years.
accepted.tq: Separate the purpose of the temples from the numerical tradition of the battles.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: At which places did Chalukya Bhima I repel the forces of Krishna II?
accepted.x: Chalukya Bhima I repelled Krishna II's forces at Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru.
accepted.tq: Use place-pair discrimination to avoid confusing Rashtrakuta battles with later Chola–Kalyani conflicts.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: After 973 CE, the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas was the
accepted.x: After 973 CE, the Kalyani Chalukyas emerged as the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas. Satyasraya and Someshvara I are associated with this later phase.
accepted.tq: Identify the change in the rival dynasty by using the chronological marker.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Chalukya Bhima I fought Krishna II, not Dhruva. Vijayaditya II fought the Rashtrakutas under Amoghavarsha, while Gunaga Vijayaditya defeated Krishna II and the Kalinga king Devendravarma.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped opponent, a standard ruler-with-deed trap.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: Jatachoda Bhima, a Telugu Choda of Pedakallu, is associated with which event?
o: Merging Vengi into the Chola Empire
Defeating Dantidurga and founding the Rashtrakuta line
Building three Shiva temples at Kalidindi
accepted.x: Jatachoda Bhima killed Danarnava and occupied Vengi. Danarnava's sons, Saktivarma I and Vimaladitya, fled to Rajaraja Chola.
accepted.tq: Link the regional ruler to his specific political action and location.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: In 1006 CE, Satyasraya sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi. Who defeated Bayyalanambi?
o: Vijayaditya VII with Rajendra Chola's assistance
accepted.x: Saktivarma I defeated Bayyalanambi with Chola help in 1006 CE. Satyasraya of the Kalyani Chalukyas had sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi.
accepted.tq: Track the combatant, the opposing commander and the external support separately.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: Coins of Saktivarma I have been found in
accepted.x: Coins of Saktivarma I have been found in Arakan, in present-day Burma.
accepted.tq: Test the unusual archaeological location directly, using nearby political centres as distractors.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Vimaladitya — Kundavva, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I
2. Vimaladitya — Melama, daughter of Jatachoda Bhima
3. Rajaraja Narendra — Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra Chola
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. Vimaladitya married both Kundavva and Melama, while Rajaraja Narendra married Ammanga Devi, the daughter of Rajendra Chola.
accepted.tq: Check each marriage independently because the same ruler is linked with two different marital alliances.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: Who supported Rajaraja Narendra in his succession war against Vijayaditya VII?
accepted.x: Rajaraja Narendra, the son of Kundavva, was supported by Rajendra I. Vijayaditya VII, the son of Melama, was supported by Kalyani Jayasimha II.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two rival claimants by matching each with his external supporter.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the battle of Kalidindi is correct?
o: The Chola army defeated Vijayaditya VII and the Kalyani army.
Rajaraja Narendra defeated Rajadhiraja I and captured Koppam.
The Rashtrakuta army defeated Rajaraja Narendra and the Chola army.
Jatachoda Bhima defeated Danarnava and occupied Kalidindi.
accepted.x: At Kalidindi, the Chola army defeated Vijayaditya VII and the Kalyani army. Rajaraja Narendra subsequently built three Shiva temples there for the fallen Chola commanders.
accepted.tq: Use the battle-location association and reject reversals of the victorious and defeated sides.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: Rajaraja Narendra built three Shiva temples at Kalidindi in memory of the
accepted.x: The three Shiva temples at Kalidindi were built by Rajaraja Narendra for the fallen Chola commanders.
accepted.tq: Identify the commemorated group rather than the dynasty that constructed the temples.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Coronation of Rajaraja Narendra
B. Vimaladitya's coronation
C. Battle of Kalidindi
D. Battle of Koppam
accepted.x: Vimaladitya was crowned in May 1011, Rajaraja Narendra in 1022, the Kalidindi conflict followed, and the battle of Koppam occurred in 1053.
accepted.tq: Place the securely dated events first and use the sequence of the succession conflict to order the remainder.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: At Koppam in 1053, who killed Rajadhiraja I?
accepted.x: Ahavamalla Someshwara killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam in 1053. Rajadhiraja had earlier won at Dharanikota and burnt Kollipaka.
accepted.tq: Match the battlefield casualty with the ruler responsible for the decisive reversal.
accepted.sec: Wars with Rashtrakutas - rulers and battles

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas in the order stated for their early and later rulers?
accepted.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana used Pithapuram as the first capital, Jayasimha Vallabha I used Vengi, and Rajamahendravaram was associated with Amma I and Rajaraja Narendra.
accepted.tq: Order capitals by ruler association rather than by present-day prominence.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s: Vengi, identified with Pedavegi near Eluru, was the capital under
accepted.x: Vengi, corresponding to Pedavegi near Eluru, was the capital under Jayasimha Vallabha I.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the capital-place association from the first and last capitals in the sequence.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s: Which rulers are associated with Rajamahendravaram as a capital?
o: Saktivarma I and Chalukya Bhima I
Kubja Vishnuvardhana and Jayasimha Vallabha I
accepted.x: Rajamahendravaram was associated with Amma I and Rajaraja Narendra. Pithapuram was the first capital, while Vengi was associated with Jayasimha Vallabha I.
accepted.tq: Pair the capital with both rulers listed for it and avoid substituting rulers from adjacent phases.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s: What was the consequence of Vijayaditya VII's death in 1075?
o: Jatachoda Bhima restored the Badami Chalukya line.
Kulottunga I merged Vengi into the Chola Empire.
Saktivarma I founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty.
Rajadhiraja I shifted the capital to Pithapuram.
accepted.x: Vijayaditya VII died in 1075, after which Kulottunga I, the son of Rajaraja Narendra, merged Vengi into the Chola Empire, creating the Chalukya-Chola line.
accepted.tq: Connect the end-of-dynasty event with its direct political consequence.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s: The Cheepurupalli inscription is associated with Kubja Vishnuvardhana's
accepted.x: The Cheepurupalli inscription of Vizianagaram is associated with Kubja Vishnuvardhana's 18th regnal year.
accepted.tq: Attach the number to the inscription's regnal-year detail, not to a military or dynastic claim.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s: The Kopparam copper plates of 631 CE describe Kubja Vishnuvardhana as
accepted.x: The Kopparam copper plates dated to 631 CE describe Kubja Vishnuvardhana as Yuvaraja.
accepted.tq: Match the dated record with the exact status or title mentioned in it.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s: Which inscription is associated with Jayasimha Vallabha?
accepted.x: The Vipparla inscription is associated with Jayasimha Vallabha. Kakumanu is associated with Chalukya Bhima I, Nandampudi with Rajaraja Narendra, and Sataluru with Vijayaditya II's temples.
accepted.tq: Use inscription–ruler matching and eliminate records belonging to neighbouring rulers.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s: Which inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with 108 temples?
accepted.x: The Sataluru inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with the 108 temples. Addanki is associated with Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription.
accepted.tq: Separate two inscription records by matching their distinctive content.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s: The Addanki inscription is notable because it is associated with
o: Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription
Chalukya Bhima I's military victory at Peruvanguru
Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu
accepted.x: The Addanki inscription is associated with Pandaranga, the general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, and is regarded as the first Telugu verse inscription.
accepted.tq: Identify the record through its unique person-and-content combination.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s:
Which of the following inscription–ruler pairs is correctly matched?
1. Kakumanu — Chalukya Bhima I
2. Nandampudi — Rajaraja Narendra
3. Korumelli plates — Rajaraja Narendra
4. Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. The Nandampudi inscription records Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu, written by Nannaya, and the Korumelli plates are also associated with Rajaraja Narendra.
accepted.tq: Confirm the sure inscription pairs first and then test the remaining records individually.
accepted.sec: Capitals and inscriptions → ruler (Pishtapura, Vengi, Rajamahendravaram; end of the line)

accepted.s: Which one of the following title–ruler pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Chalukya Chandra was the title of Saktivarma I, not Vimaladitya. Vimaladitya bore the titles Rajamartanda and Mummadi Bhima.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped ruler in a title table, especially where two rulers belong to the same dynastic phase.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler

accepted.s: The titles Tribhuvanankusa and Samasta Bhuvanashraya are associated with
o: Vijayaditya II and Gunaga Vijayaditya III
accepted.x: The titles Tribhuvanankusa and Samasta Bhuvanashraya are associated with Jayasimha I and Vishnuvardhana III.
accepted.tq: Match the shared title group with the two rulers instead of assigning each title to a single later king.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler

accepted.s: Who bore the title Narendramrigaraja?
accepted.x: Vijayaditya II bore the title Narendramrigaraja. Rajaraja Narendra bore the titles Kavyageetha Priyudu and Rajarajanarayana.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar royal names and the titles attached to them.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler

accepted.s: According to the APPSC key, the victories commemorated by the title Tripura-martya-Maheswara were over
accepted.x: The APPSC key identifies Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and Kandukur as the three cities. This triplet is associated with Gunaga Vijayaditya III's title Tripura-martya-Maheswara.
accepted.tq: Use the officially keyed triplet and distinguish it from the commonly confused alternative list.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler

accepted.s: Which ruler is associated with the title Rajamahendra?
accepted.x: Ammaraja I bore the title Rajamahendra. Rajaraja Narendra bore the titles Kavyageetha Priyudu and Rajarajanarayana.
accepted.tq: Separate similar-looking names such as Amma, Ammaraja and Rajaraja before matching the title.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Chalukya Bhima — Kollabhiganda
2. Saktivarma I — Chalukya Chandra
3. Vimaladitya — Rajamartanda
4. Rajaraja Narendra — Rajarajanarayana
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Chalukya Bhima was associated with Kollabhiganda, Saktivarma I with Chalukya Chandra, Vimaladitya with Rajamartanda, and Rajaraja Narendra with Rajarajanarayana.
accepted.tq: Verify each title pair independently and watch for the common Kollabhiganda attribution trap.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler

accepted.s: The title Rajamartanda, along with Mummadi Bhima, was borne by
accepted.x: Vimaladitya bore the titles Rajamartanda and Mummadi Bhima. Chalukya Bhima is associated with the title Kollabhiganda.
accepted.tq: Distinguish titles of similarly named rulers by grouping the paired epithets.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler

accepted.s: Which title–ruler association is correctly stated?
accepted.x: Kavyageetha Priyudu was a title of Rajaraja Narendra. Vishamasiddhi belonged to Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Narendramrigaraja to Vijayaditya II, and Rajamahendra to Ammaraja I.
accepted.tq: Use elimination among neighbouring title associations and reject swapped ruler names.
accepted.sec: Titles → ruler

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Inscription or grant)
a. Kopparam
b. Vipparla
c. Chekurru

d. Chipurupalli

List-II (Associated ruler or person)
i. Ammaraja I
ii. Kubja Vishnuvardhana

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Kopparam is associated with Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Vipparla with Jayasimha I, Chekurru with Ammaraja I, and Chipurupalli names the scholar Madhavasharma.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure inscription–ruler pair and then complete the one-to-one matching.

accepted.s: The Chekurru copper-plate grant is associated with
accepted.x: The Chekurru copper-plate grant is associated with Ammaraja I. Vipparla is associated with Jayasimha I and Kopparam with Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
accepted.tq: Test a single grant–ruler association directly while using nearby grants as distractors.
accepted.sec: Copper-plate grants → ruler

accepted.s: The Kopparam copper plates are associated with which ruler in the copper-plate grant tradition?
accepted.x: In the copper-plate grant association, the Kopparam plates are attributed to Pulakesin II. The separate Kopparam record dated 631 CE describes Kubja Vishnuvardhana as Yuvaraja.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similarly named or located records instead of merging their attributions.
accepted.sec: Copper-plate grants → ruler

accepted.s: Which scholar is named in the Chipurupalli inscription?
accepted.x: The Chipurupalli inscription names the scholar Madhavasharma. Narayana Bhattu and Nannaya are associated with the Nandampudi record, while Pandaranga is associated with Addanki.
accepted.tq: Separate the named scholar from other literary and military figures in the inscription list.
accepted.sec: Copper-plate grants → ruler
